quote_check_note: All 29 first-reader quotes were matched against ROOT/pdf/P-1407.txt and ROOT/pdf/P-1267.txt on the page stated, after collapsing whitespace (the table-row quotes span one cell per line in the extract). The P-1407 p.4 pTau181 sentence matches only with its line break after 'MCI-' joined. The table-row readings were also checked against the column order of Table 1 (P-1407) and Table 3 (P-1267): the unadjusted block precedes the adjusted block, and the adjusted top-quartile figures match the text on p.6.
strongest_case_against_the_verdict: Set P-1407's MCI-AD subgroup, the part of the Newcastle cohort closest to BALTAZAR (P-1267 excluded Lewy body, parkinsonian, frontotemporal and vascular MCI, and 96% of its converters went to probable AD), against P-1267's continuous ratio. P-1407 gives HR 0.67 (0.37-1.20) per control-referenced SD of the inverted ratio, so a more abnormal (lower) Abeta42/40 goes with a LOWER hazard. P-1267 gives HR 0.95 (0.91-0.99) for the free ratio and 0.92 (0.86-0.98) for the total ratio per percentage point, so a lower ratio goes with a HIGHER hazard. Put P-1267 on a per-SD scale using its own printed sample SDs (free 20.4 +/- 7.3, total 13.9 +/- 4.5 percentage points, Table 2): per SD lower ratio, about 1.45 (1.08-1.99) free and 1.46 (1.10-1.97) total (my computation). On that scale P-1407's MCI-AD interval excludes P-1267's point estimate, P-1267's interval excludes P-1407's point estimate, and a z-test of the difference in log hazard ratios gives z of about 2.3 (p of about 0.02). The dataset-family mismatch (Newcastle vs BALTAZAR) could plausibly be waived on the C-232 precedent, which waived a cross-cohort difference. Read as 'a point estimate outside the other study's interval', this is an incompatibility on a quantity the ledger record never named.
why_it_does_or_does_not_succeed: It does not succeed under the rule as written. (1) The rescaled intervals still overlap (P-1407 0.37-1.20 against P-1267 from 1.08 or 1.10 upward), and they keep overlapping unless one Newcastle control SD on the Simoa scale corresponded to more than about two BALTAZAR MCI-sample SDs on the INNO-BIA scale (about 2.0 for the total ratio, 2.5 for the free ratio), which nothing in either paper suggests. CONFLICT_BRIEF says significant vs non-significant 'with overlapping intervals' is not incompatible, so 'reported uncertainty excludes the other' cannot be met by a point estimate falling outside the other interval while the intervals overlap. (2) P-1407's MCI-AD direction has no support from its own statistics (p = 0.180), so the 'opposite directions each supported by the study's own statistics' limb fails. (3) The per-SD scale is my construction, not reported uncertainty: P-1407 standardises blood results to the control mean without printing the control SD, uses another platform (Simoa, against INNO-BIA free and total fractions) and inverts the ratio; no interval printed by either paper excludes the other. The z-test is a heterogeneity test the rule does not use, and it is fragile: its p-value rises to about 0.06 if the control SD is half the BALTAZAR SD, and to about 0.07 with P-1267's unadjusted estimate. (4) The covariate-conditional estimands differ in a way that bears on the result: P-1267's continuous association is significant only with APOE e4 in the model (unadjusted free ratio HR 0.97, 0.93-1.02, p = 0.21, about 1.25, 0.87-1.70, per SD), whereas P-1407 adjusts for MMSE. In BALTAZAR itself, MMSE predicts conversion strongly (HR 0.85 per point, p = 0.0002) and was higher in the top quartile of the total ratio (p = 0.046); P-1267 prints no MMSE-adjusted model. (5) The endpoints differ: P-1407 uses dementia or death with no fixed horizon; P-1267 uses adjudicated dementia, censored at 36 months or the last visit. In addition, P-1407's MCI-AD group is assigned from the final diagnosis after follow-up (n = 43, 21 events). (6) The whole-cohort (1.06) and probable MCI-LB (1.23) estimates point the same way as P-1267, and their intervals overlap P-1267's on any scaling. The other alternative, documented_incommensurability, rests on the operator's C-234 reclassification, which listed 'different quantities' before 'compatible results'. It does not displace false_positive: CONFLICT_BRIEF applies false_positive first, and two of its limbs are met. The results are compatible (the difference is one of significance), and the record misreads P-1407 (it calls the 72 dementia-or-death events conversions, treats non-significant hazard ratios as 'no prognostic value', and its review note says no HR, CI or p-value exists). Either way the pair is not genuine. The first reader's grounds stand; I add the rescaling test above because it is the obvious counter-argument and the verdict survives it. The first reader's hypothetical item (d), the dataset-family gate, is the weakest of their four incommensurability items because a cross-cohort waiver has precedent (C-232), but items (a) to (c) carry that hypothetical without it.
grounds: P-1407 prints Abeta42/40 hazard ratios for all three groups, and with the ratio inverted so that higher means more abnormal, the whole-cohort (1.06, 0.83-1.35) and probable MCI-LB (1.23, 0.94-1.60) estimates point the same way as P-1267's protective high ratio.
The only opposite estimate, MCI-AD 0.67 (0.37-1.20, p = 0.180), is not supported by P-1407's own statistics, so no pair of opposite directions is each statistically supported.

Rescaled with P-1267's own printed sample SDs, P-1267's continuous hazard ratios (about 1.45 per SD lower ratio, lower limits about 1.08 to 1.10) overlap P-1407's MCI-AD interval under any plausible scaling, so the rule's overlapping-intervals clause makes this a difference in significance, not an incompatibility.

P-1267's continuous association depends on APOE e4 adjustment (unadjusted free ratio HR 0.97, 0.93-1.02, p = 0.21), whereas P-1407 adjusts for MMSE, which strongly predicts conversion in BALTAZAR itself, so the covariate-conditional estimands differ.

The endpoints differ (dementia or death in P-1407; adjudicated dementia censored at 36 months in P-1267), and P-1407's MCI-AD group is assigned from the final diagnosis after follow-up, while BALTAZAR excluded non-AD MCI at baseline.
The record misreads P-1407: its 72 events are dementia-or-death events, not conversions, and its non-significant hazard ratios are recast as 'no prognostic value'.
The dataset-family gate fails with no waiver on record; a waiver on the C-232 precedent is conceivable but would not cure the grounds above.

evidence_quote_note: Evidence quotes are verbatim from the regenerated pack extracts, allowing for whitespace collapse and for words hyphenated across a line break (P-1407 p.4 'devia-tions' read as 'deviations'). The per-SD figures, the overlap threshold and the z-tests are my computations from the printed hazard ratios, intervals and sample SDs; neither paper reports them.
corrections_to_first_reader: what_each_reports and ground 3 say the authors attribute the MCI-AD nulls to 43 cases and 21 events; P-1407 (p.4) gives that explanation only for the absent pTau181 association and offers none for Abeta42/40. The quote cited is accurate; the paraphrase generalises it.

quantity_a describes P-1407's measurement as 'Simoa, total peptide'; P-1407 does not say whether its Simoa Abeta40/42 values correspond to a free or a total fraction, so 'total peptide' is an inference.

Ground 5 says P-1267 grouped the lower quartiles 'after inspection'. The Results (p.6) do give an observed-pattern reason, but the Methods (p.5) announce the highest-quartile-versus-rest analysis in advance, citing the gradient seen in Hanon et al. (2022) in the same cohort.

what_each_reports says P-1267's one death was 'not counted as an event'. The paper reports the death (p.5) without saying how it was handled; censoring at the last visit follows from its Methods (p.4) but is not stated for that participant.
